name: Solar on Flat and Low-Slope Roofs in Los Angeles County: What to Know

mainEntity.name: What special considerations apply to solar installation on flat or low-slope roofs in Los Angeles County?
mainEntity.text: What special considerations apply to solar installation on flat or low-slope roofs in Los Angeles County?

acceptedAnswer.text: Flat and low-slope roofs, common on many Los Angeles County homes and multifamily buildings, pose different challenges than pitched roofs. Mounting options include ballasted systems that rely on weight and systems anchored into the structure, each with pros and cons. Ballasted arrays reduce penetrations but add roof load and require careful engineering for wind uplift. Attached systems create penetrations that must be flashed flawlessly to protect the roof membrane and preserve warranties. Water drainage and ponding areas are critical. Panels and racking should not block drains or sit in standing water zones. Slightly tilted racking improves energy production, helps dirt and debris shed, and eases maintenance, but it can increase wind forces and visual impact from the street or neighboring buildings. Before proceeding, obtain your roof’s structural and membrane details and share them with the installer. Ask for an engineering review that considers weight, wind, and local codes. Confirm that the mounting method and flashing are approved by your roofing manufacturer and that any roof warranties will remain intact. Clear coordination between the roofer and solar contractor minimizes leak risks and ensures the design respects both structural and waterproofing needs.
acceptedAnswer.description: Flat and low-slope roofs in Los Angeles County require attention to ballast or attachment methods, drainage, wind loading, and roof warranty compatibility. Tilted racking improves performance and cleaning but can increase visibility and engineering complexity, so a tailored design that respects roof membrane and ponding areas is essential.
